sentences.zh: 姚泓

translations.literal: Section heading: Yao Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong.

sentences.zh: 姚泓，字元子，興之長子也。

translations.literal: Yao Hong, courtesy name Yuanzi, was the eldest son of Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong, whose courtesy name was Yuanzi, was Yao Xing’s eldest son.

sentences.zh: 孝友寬和，而無經世之用，又多疾病，興將以為嗣而疑焉。

translations.literal: He was filial, affectionate toward his brothers, generous and mild, yet lacked the ability to govern the realm and was often ill. Xing intended to make him heir but hesitated.
translations.idiomatic: He was dutiful to his parents, affectionate toward his brothers, generous and mild. But he lacked the ability to govern and was often ill, so Yao Xing hesitated over making him heir.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃立為太子。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was then established as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At length Yao Xing named him crown prince.

sentences.zh: 興每征伐巡遊，常留總後事。

translations.literal: Whenever Xing on campaign or inspection tour, he regularly left him behind to oversee rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yao Xing marched or toured, he left Yao Hong in charge of the rear.

sentences.zh: 博學善談論，尤好詩詠。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned and good at discourse, especially fond of poetry and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned, a fluent talker, and especially loved poetry.

sentences.zh: 尚書王尚、黃門郎段章、尚書郎富允文以儒術侍講，胡義周、夏侯稚以文章遊集。

translations.literal: Master of Writing Wang Shang, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates Duan Zhang, and gentleman of the Department of State Affairs Fu Yunwen attended him as lecturers on Confucian learning. Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi joined him in literary gatherings.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shang, a master of writing, Duan Zhang, a gentleman of the Yellow Gates, and Fu Yunwen, a gentleman of the Department of State Affairs, tutored him in the classics. Hu Yizhou and Xiahou Zhi joined him for literary gatherings.

sentences.zh: 時尚書王敏、右丞郭播以刑政過寬，議欲峻制，泓曰：「人情挫辱，則壯厲之心生；

translations.literal: At the time, Master of Writing Wang Min and Right Assistant Director Guo Bo considered the administration of punishments too lenient and discussed imposing stricter rules. Hong said, “When people are thwarted and humiliated, a fierce spirit rises in them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Min, a master of writing, and Guo Bo, the right assistant director, thought the administration of punishments too lenient and proposed stricter regulations. Yao Hong replied, “Humiliate people and you breed defiance.

sentences.zh: 政教煩苛，則苟免之行立。

translations.literal: When government and instruction are fussy and harsh, conduct of bare escape is established.
translations.idiomatic: Smother them in petty rules and they learn only to dodge.

sentences.zh: 上之化下，如風靡草。

translations.literal: What is above transforms what is below, like wind bending grass.
translations.idiomatic: Those above shape those below as wind bends grass.

sentences.zh: 君等參贊朝化，弘昭政軌，不務仁恕之道，惟欲嚴法酷刑，豈是安上馭下之理乎！」

translations.literal: You gentlemen assist and join in court transformation, broadly display the tracks of government—if you do not pursue the way of benevolence and forgiveness, but only desire harsh laws and cruel punishments, how could that be the principle of quieting those above and controlling those below!"
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen help guide the court and make its principles of government known. If you neglect humanity and clemency and seek only strict laws and cruel punishments, how can you keep the ruler secure and govern his subjects?”

sentences.zh: 敏等遂止。

translations.literal: Min and others then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Min and his allies dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 泓受經于博士淳于岐。

translations.literal: Hong received the classics from Erudite Chunyu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong studied the classics under the erudite Chunyu Qi.

sentences.zh: 岐病，泓親詣省疾，拜於床下。

translations.literal: When Qi was ill, Hong personally went to inquire after his illness and bowed below the couch.
translations.idiomatic: When Chunyu Qi fell ill, Yao Hong visited his bedside and bowed on the floor.

sentences.zh: 自是公侯見師傅皆拜焉。

translations.literal: From this dukes and marquises seeing tutors all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: After that, dukes and marquises all bowed when they met their tutors.

sentences.zh: 興之如平涼也，馮翊人劉厥聚眾數千，據萬年以叛。

translations.literal: When Xing went to Pingliang, a man of Fengyi, Liu Jue, gathered several thousand followers, occupied Wannian, and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing marched to Pingliang, Liu Jue of Fengyi raised several thousand men, seized Wannian, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 泓遣鎮軍彭白狼率東宮禁兵討之，斬厥，赦其餘黨。

translations.literal: Hong sent General Who Guards the Army Peng Bailang to lead eastern-palace household troops to campaign against him, beheaded Jue, and pardoned the rest of the faction.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Peng Bailang, the General Who Guards the Army, to lead the Eastern Palace guards against Liu Jue. Jue was beheaded and the remaining rebels pardoned.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸勸泓曰：「殿下神算電發，蕩平醜逆，宜露布表言，廣其首級，以慰遠近之情。」

translations.literal: All the generals urged Hong, “Your Highness’s inspired plans flashed forth like lightning and swept away the vile rebels. You should report the victory in an open dispatch, inflating the tally of severed heads to reassure people far and near.”
translations.idiomatic: All the generals urged Hong, “Your Highness devised your plans with lightning speed and swept away the vile rebels. You should issue an open dispatch reporting the victory and claiming a greater number of enemy heads, to reassure people far and near.”

sentences.zh: 泓曰：「主上委吾後事，使式遏寇逆。

translations.literal: Hong said, "The lord above entrusted me with rear affairs, making me check invading rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong answered: "My father left me the rear to stop traitors.

sentences.zh: 吾綏禦失和，以長奸寇，方當引咎責躬，歸罪行間，安敢過自矜誕，以重罪責乎！」

translations.literal: I failed to strike the right balance in pacifying and defending the people, and so encouraged the rebels. I ought now to take the blame, reproach myself and acknowledge my guilt before the ranks. How dare I boast extravagantly and make my fault still greater?”
translations.idiomatic: I failed to strike the right balance in pacifying and defending the people, and so encouraged the rebels. I ought now to take the blame, reproach myself and acknowledge my guilt before the ranks. How dare I boast extravagantly and make my fault still greater?”

sentences.zh: 其右僕射韋華聞而謂河南太守慕容築曰：「皇太子實有恭惠之德，社稷之福也。」

translations.literal: His right vice-director Wei Hua heard it and said to Henan Grand Administrator Murong Zhu, "The crown prince truly has the virtue of reverence and kindness—blessing for the altars."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of this, Wei Hua, the right vice-director, told Murong Zhu, governor of Henan, “The crown prince truly is respectful and kind. That is a blessing for the state.”

sentences.zh: 其弟弼有奪嫡之謀，泓恩撫如初，未嘗見於色。

translations.literal: His younger brother Bi had a plan to seize the heirship; Hong treated him with favor as at first and never showed it in his expression.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yao Bi plotted to supplant him, yet Yao Hong treated him with unchanged kindness and never showed resentment.

sentences.zh: 姚紹每為弼羽翼，泓亦推心宗事，弗以為嫌。

translations.literal: Yao Shao repeatedly supported Bi, yet Hong trusted Shao wholeheartedly, treated him with the deference due a senior kinsman and bore him no grudge on that account.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao repeatedly supported Bi, yet Hong trusted Shao wholeheartedly, treated him with the deference due a senior kinsman and bore him no grudge on that account.

sentences.zh: 及僭立，任紹以兵權，紹亦感而歸誠，卒守其忠烈。

translations.literal: When he presumptuously mounted the throne, he entrusted Shao with military authority; Shao was also moved and returned sincerity, and in the end kept his loyal fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Hong claimed the imperial throne, he entrusted Yao Shao with military command. Moved by this, Shao pledged himself to Hong and remained loyal to the end.

sentences.zh: 其明識寬裕，皆此類也。

translations.literal: His clear insight and generous breadth were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His judgment and magnanimity ran in that vein throughout.

sentences.zh: 興既死，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: After Xing died, they secretly did not issue mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing died, the court hid the news.

sentences.zh: 南陽公姚愔及大將軍尹元等謀為亂，泓皆誅之。

translations.literal: Duke of Nanyang Yao Yin and Grand General Yin Yuan and others plotted rebellion; Hong executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yin, Duke of Nanyang, Grand General Yin Yuan and others plotted rebellion. Yao Hong put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 命其齊公姚恢殺安定太守呂超，恢久乃誅之。

translations.literal: He ordered Duke of Qi Yao Hui to kill Anding Grand Administrator Lü Chao; Hui long delayed before killing him.
translations.idiomatic: He told Duke Qi Yao Hui to kill Lü Chao, governor of Anding; Yao Hui dragged his feet before obeying.

sentences.zh: 泓疑恢有陰謀，恢自是懷貳，陰聚兵甲焉。

translations.literal: Hong suspected Hui had a hidden plot; Hui from this harbored two minds and secretly gathered armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong suspected treason; Yao Hui began to hedge and stockpile arms in secret.

sentences.zh: 泓發喪，以義熙十二年僭即帝位，大赦殊死已下，改元永和，廬於諮議堂。

translations.literal: Hong announced the mourning. In the twelfth year of Yixi he presumptuously ascended the imperial throne, proclaimed a general pardon extending to those condemned to death, changed the era name to Yonghe and lodged in a mourning hut at the council hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong announced the mourning. In the twelfth year of Yixi he claimed the imperial throne, issued a general pardon extending even to those condemned to death, changed the era name to Yonghe and took up quarters in a mourning hut at the council hall.

sentences.zh: 既葬，乃親庶政，內外百僚增位一等，令文武各盡直言，政有不便於時，事有光益宗廟者，極言勿有所諱。

translations.literal: After burial, he then personally attended to myriad government; inner and outer hundred officials were raised one rank in position; he ordered civil and military each to exhaust straight speech—where government had what was not convenient to the time, or affairs that could add lustre to the ancestral temple, speak to the utmost without hiding.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial Hong took charge of government himself and promoted every official at court and in the provinces by one rank. He ordered civil and military officers alike to speak freely about policies unsuited to the times and measures that would bring honor and benefit to the dynasty, holding nothing back.

sentences.zh: 初，興徙李閏羌三千家于安定，尋徙新支。

translations.literal: At first, Xing had moved three thousand households of Li-run Qiang to Anding, then soon moved them to Xin-zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing had earlier moved three thousand Li-run Qiang households to Anding, then shifted them again to Xin-zhi.

sentences.zh: 至是，羌酋党容率所部叛還，遣撫軍姚贊討之。

translations.literal: At this point, Qiang chief Dang Rong led his following in revolt to return; he sent General Who Pacifies Yao Zan to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang chief Dang Rong then led his followers in revolt and set out for home. Yao Hong sent Pacifying General Yao Zan to attack him.

sentences.zh: 容降，徙其豪右數百戶于長安，余遣還李閏。

translations.literal: Rong surrendered; he moved several hundred notable households to Chang'an and sent the rest back to Li-run.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Rong surrendered. Yao Hong moved several hundred of the leading households to Chang’an and sent the rest back to Lirun.

sentences.zh: 北地太守毛雍據趙氏塢以叛于泓，姚紹討擒之。

translations.literal: Beidi Grand Administrator Mao Yong occupied the Zhao clan stockade and rebelled against Hong; Yao Shao campaigned, seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yong, governor of Beidi, occupied the Zhao clan’s stockade in revolt against Yao Hong. Yao Shao attacked and captured him.

sentences.zh: 姚宣時鎮李閏，未知雍敗，遣部將姚佛生等來衛長安。

translations.literal: Yao Xuan then garrisoned Li-run, not yet knowing of Yong's defeat, sent subordinate generals Yao Fosheng and others to come guard Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xuan was then garrisoning Lirun and had not yet learned that Mao Yong had been defeated, so he sent his subordinate commander Yao Fosheng and others to defend Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 眾既發，宣參軍韋宗奸諂好亂，說宣曰：「主上初立，威化末著，勃勃強盛，侵害必深，本朝之難未可弭也。

translations.literal: Once the host had set out, Xuan's adviser Wei Zong, fawning and fond of turmoil, spoke to Xuan, saying, "The lord has just risen, awe and transformation are not yet manifest; Bobo is strong and flourishing, harm and invasion will surely be deep; the hardship of this court is not yet to be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops had set out, Yao Xuan’s adviser Wei Zong, a deceitful flatterer who delighted in disorder, urged him, “The ruler has only just taken the throne, and his authority is not yet established. Helian Bobo is powerful, and his incursions are sure to cause great harm. Our court’s troubles cannot yet be put to rest.

sentences.zh: 殿下居維城之任，宜深慮之。

translations.literal: Your Highness holds the responsibility of a bulwark of the ruling house. You should consider this deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has the duty of protecting the ruling house. You should consider this carefully.

sentences.zh: 邢望地形險固，總三方之要，若能據之，虛心撫禦，非但克固維城，亦霸王之業也。」

translations.literal: Xingwang's terrain is perilous and firm, gathering the key of three directions—if you can occupy it, with empty mind soothe and control, not only can you solidify the bulwark, it is also the enterprise of a hegemon-king."
translations.idiomatic: Xingwang is naturally defensible and commands the approaches from three directions. If you occupy it and govern the people there with an open mind, you can secure your position as a bulwark of the dynasty and even lay the foundations of a hegemon’s or a king’s rule.”

sentences.zh: 宣乃率戶三萬八千，棄李閏，南保邢望。

translations.literal: Xuan then led thirty-eight thousand households, abandoned Li-run, and went south to hold Xingwang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xuan abandoned Lirun and led thirty-eight thousand households south to hold Xingwang.

sentences.zh: 宣既南移，諸羌據李閏以叛，紹進討破之。

translations.literal: Once Xuan had moved south, the various Qiang occupied Li-run in revolt; Shao advanced and campaigned, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yao Xuan had moved south, the Qiang groups occupied Lirun in revolt. Yao Shao advanced against them and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 宣詣紹歸罪，紹怒殺之。

translations.literal: Xuan went to Shao to confess guilt; Shao in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xuan went to Yao Shao to acknowledge his guilt. Shao killed him in anger.

sentences.zh: 初，宣在邢望，泓遣姚佛生諭宣，佛生遂贊成宣計。

translations.literal: At first, while Xuan was at Xingwang, Hong sent Yao Fosheng to instruct Xuan; Fosheng then endorsed Xuan's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yao Xuan was at Xingwang, Yao Hong had sent Yao Fosheng to reason with him. Fosheng ended up supporting Xuan’s plan.

sentences.zh: 紹數其罪，又戮之。

translations.literal: Shao enumerated his crimes and executed him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao listed Fosheng's crimes and put him to death too.

sentences.zh: 泓下書，士卒死王事，贈以爵位，永復其家。

translations.literal: Hong issued a document: soldiers who died in the king's service were granted rank and title, and their families were forever exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong decreed that soldiers who died in royal service should receive posthumous titles and their families should enjoy perpetual exemption from levies.

sentences.zh: 將封宮臣十六人五等子男，姚贊諫曰：「東宮文武，自當有守忠之誠，未有赫然之效，何受封之多乎？」

translations.literal: He was about to enfeoff sixteen palace officials as viscounts and barons in the five grades of nobility. Yao Zan remonstrated, “The Eastern Palace’s civil and military officers naturally owe it faithful loyalty. They have yet to show conspicuous merit. Why should they receive so many grants of fiefs?”
translations.idiomatic: Hong proposed making sixteen palace officers viscounts or barons under the five-rank system of nobility. Yao Zan objected, “Surely the crown prince’s civil and military officers owe him loyalty as a matter of duty. They have shown no conspicuous merit. Why grant them so many fiefs?”

sentences.zh: 泓曰：「懸爵於朝，所以懲勸來效，標明盛德。

translations.literal: Hong said, "Suspending rank in court is to punish and encourage coming merit and mark splendid virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong replied, “The court holds out titles to admonish and encourage those who will render service and to give public recognition to outstanding virtue.

sentences.zh: 元子遭家不造，與宮臣同此百憂，獨享其福，得不愧於心乎！」

translations.literal: Yuanzi meets the house in misfortune, sharing every worry with palace officials—how could he alone enjoy the blessing without shame in heart!"
translations.idiomatic: I, Yuanzi, have seen my house struck by misfortune. My palace officers shared all these troubles with me. Could I enjoy the good fortune alone without feeling ashamed?”

sentences.zh: 贊默然。

translations.literal: Zan was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan held his tongue.

sentences.zh: 姚紹進曰：「陛下不忘報德，封之是也，古者敬其事，命之以始，可須來春，然後議之。」

translations.literal: Yao Shao stepped forward and said, “Your Majesty remembers to repay virtue; enfeoffing them is right. The ancients treated such matters with reverence and made appointments at the beginning of the year. You could wait until next spring and then consider it.”
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao stepped forward. “Your Majesty remembers to reward virtue, and you are right to grant them fiefs. In antiquity people treated such matters with reverence, timing the appointments for the beginning of the year. You could wait until next spring and then deliberate.”

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 并州、定陽、貳城胡數萬落叛泓，入於平陽，攻立義姚成都於匈奴堡，推匈奴曹弘為大單于，所在殘掠。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands of Hu households from Bingzhou, Dingyang and Ercheng rebelled against Hong. They entered Pingyang, attacked General Yao Chengdu, who held the title Liyi, at the Xiongnu fort, and proclaimed Cao Hong of the Xiongnu grand shanyu. Everywhere they went they ravaged and plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of thousands of Hu households from Bingzhou, Dingyang and Ercheng rebelled against Hong. They entered Pingyang, attacked General Yao Chengdu, who held the title Liyi, at the Xiongnu fort, and proclaimed Cao Hong of the Xiongnu grand shanyu. Everywhere they went they ravaged and plundered.

sentences.zh: 征東姚懿自蒲阪討弘，戰於平陽，大破之，執弘，送于長安，徙其豪右萬五千落於雍州。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the East Yao Yi set out from Puban against Cao Hong. He fought at Pingyang, routed Hong, captured him and sent him to Chang’an. He transferred fifteen thousand of their leading households to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi, General Who Conquers the East, marched from Puban against Cao Hong, routed him at Pingyang, captured him and sent him to Chang’an. Yi resettled fifteen thousand leading households in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 仇池公楊盛攻陷祁山，執建節王總，遂逼秦州。

translations.literal: Yang Sheng, Duke of Chouchi, stormed Qishan, captured General Wang Zong, who held the title Jianjie, and pressed on toward Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng, Duke of Chouchi, stormed Qishan, captured General Wang Zong, who held the title Jianjie, and pressed on toward Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 泓遣後將軍姚平救之，盛引退。

translations.literal: Hong sent Rear General Yao Ping to its relief, and Sheng withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Rear General Yao Ping to relieve Qinzhou, and Yang Sheng withdrew.

sentences.zh: 姚嵩與平追盛及於竹嶺，姚贊率隴西太守姚秦都、略陽太守王煥以禁兵赴之。

translations.literal: Yao Song and Yao Ping pursued Yang Sheng and caught up with him at Bamboo Ridge. Yao Zan hurried to their aid with Yao Qindu, governor of Longxi, Wang Huan, governor of Lüeyang, and the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Song and Yao Ping pursued Yang Sheng and caught up with him at Bamboo Ridge. Yao Zan hurried to their aid with Yao Qindu, governor of Longxi, Wang Huan, governor of Lüeyang, and the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 贊至清水，嵩為盛所敗，嵩及秦都、王煥皆戰死。

translations.literal: When Zan reached Qingshui, Song was defeated by Sheng; Song and Qindu and Wang Huan all died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Zan reached Qingshui, Yang Sheng defeated Yao Song. Song, Yao Qindu and Wang Huan all died in battle.

sentences.zh: 贊至秦州，退還仇池。

translations.literal: When Yao Zan reached Qinzhou, Yang Sheng withdrew to Chouchi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Zan reached Qinzhou, Yang Sheng withdrew to Chouchi.

sentences.zh: 先是，天水冀縣石鼓鳴，聲聞數百里，野雉皆雊。

translations.literal: Before this, in Tianshui Jixian a stone drum sounded, heard for several hundred li, and wild pheasants all crowed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a stone drum had sounded in Ji county, Tianshui. It could be heard for several hundred li, and the wild pheasants all crowed.

sentences.zh: 秦州地震者三十二，殷殷有聲者八，山崩舍壞，咸以為不祥。

translations.literal: In Qinzhou there were thirty-two earthquakes with rumbling sound in eight cases; mountains collapsed and houses ruined—all thought it inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzhou suffered thirty-two earthquakes, eight accompanied by rumbling. Mountains collapsed and houses fell. Everyone took these as ill omens.

sentences.zh: 及嵩將出，群僚固諫止之。

translations.literal: When Song was about to set out, the host of officials firmly remonstrated to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Song prepared to march, the court begged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 嵩曰：「若有不祥，此乃命也，安所逃乎！」

translations.literal: Song said, "If there is inauspiciousness, this is fate—where would one flee!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao Song said, "If doom comes, it is fate—there is no escape."

sentences.zh: 遂及於難。

translations.literal: Thereupon he met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He rode to his death.

sentences.zh: 識者以為秦州泓之故鄉，將滅之征也。

translations.literal: Those who understood the signs thought that, because Qinzhou was Yao Hong’s native place, they foretold his impending downfall.
translations.idiomatic: Those who understood the signs thought that, because Qinzhou was Yao Hong’s native place, they foretold his impending downfall.

sentences.zh: 赫連勃勃攻陷陰密，執秦州刺史姚軍都，坑將士五千餘人。

translations.literal: Helian Bobo attacked and took Yinmi, seized Qinzhou Inspector Yao Jundu, and buried alive more than five thousand officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Bobo stormed Yinmi, captured Yao Jundu, inspector of Qinzhou, and buried alive more than five thousand officers and men.

sentences.zh: 軍都瞋目厲聲數勃勃殘忍之罪，不為之屈，勃勃怒而殺之。

translations.literal: Jundu glared with eyes and in stern voice enumerated Bobo's crimes of cruelty and refused to yield to him; Bobo in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Jundu glared at Bobo, loudly denounced his cruelty and refused to submit. Bobo killed him in a rage.

sentences.zh: 勃勃既克陰密，進兵侵雍，嶺北雜戶悉奔五將山。

translations.literal: Once Bobo had taken Yinmi, he advanced troops to invade Yong; north-of-the-ridge miscellaneous households all fled to Five-General Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Yinmi, Bobo advanced on Yong. The mixed households north of the ridge all fled to Five Generals Mountain.

sentences.zh: 征北姚恢棄安定，率戶五千奔新平，安定人胡儼、華韜等率眾距恢，恢單騎歸長安。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the North Yao Hui abandoned Anding, led five thousand households to flee to Xinping; Anding men Hu Yan and Hua Tao led hosts to block Hui; Hui alone on horseback returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hui, General Who Conquers the North, abandoned Anding and fled toward Xinping with five thousand households. Hu Yan, Hua Tao and others from Anding led their followers against him, and Hui returned to Chang’an alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 立節彌姐成、建武裴岐為儼所殺，鎮西姚諶委鎮東走。

translations.literal: Hu Yan killed the generals Mijie Cheng and Pei Qi, holders of the titles Lijie and Jianwu respectively. Yao Chen, General Who Guards the West, abandoned his garrison and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yan killed the generals Mijie Cheng and Pei Qi, holders of the titles Lijie and Jianwu respectively. Yao Chen, General Who Guards the West, abandoned his garrison and fled east.

sentences.zh: 勃勃遂據雍，抄掠郿城。

translations.literal: Bobo thereupon occupied Yong, raiding and plundering Mei city.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo then overran Yong and raided Mei.

sentences.zh: 姚紹及征虜尹昭、鎮軍姚洽等率步騎五萬討勃勃，姚恢以精騎一萬繼之。

translations.literal: Yao Shao, General Who Campaigns against the Enemy Yin Zhao, General Who Guards the Army Yao Qia and others led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry against Bobo. Yao Hui followed with ten thousand picked cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao, General Who Campaigns against the Enemy Yin Zhao, General Who Guards the Army Yao Qia and others led fifty thousand infantry and cavalry against Bobo. Yao Hui followed with ten thousand picked cavalry.

sentences.zh: 軍次橫水，勃勃退保安定，胡儼閉門距之，殺鮮卑數千人，據安定以降。

translations.literal: The army halted at Hengshui; Bobo withdrew to guard Anding; Hu Yan closed the gate to block him, killed several thousand Xianbei, and occupied Anding to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shao’s army halted at Hengshui. Bobo fell back toward Anding, hoping to hold it, but Hu Yan shut the gates against him, killed several thousand Xianbei and surrendered Anding to Qin.

sentences.zh: 紹進兵躡勃勃，戰於馬鞍阪，敗之，追至朝那，不及而還。

translations.literal: Yao Shao pressed after Bobo, defeated him at Ma’an Slope and pursued him as far as Chaona. Unable to overtake him, Shao returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao pressed after Bobo, defeated him at Ma’an Slope and pursued him as far as Chaona. Unable to overtake him, Shao returned.

sentences.zh: 楊盛遣兄子倦入寇長蛇。

translations.literal: Yang Sheng sent his elder brother's son Juan to invade Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng sent Yang Juan, his elder brother’s son, to invade Changshe.

sentences.zh: 平陽氐苟渴聚眾千餘，據五丈原以叛，遣鎮遠姚萬、恢武姚難討之，為渴所敗。

translations.literal: Pingyang Di Gou Ke gathered more than a thousand, occupied Wuzhangyuan in revolt; he sent General Who Guards the Distance Yao Wan and General Who Restores Might Yao Nan to campaign against him, and they were defeated by Ke.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Ke, a Di man of Pingyang, gathered more than a thousand men and occupied Wuzhangyuan in revolt. Yao Hong sent Yao Wan, General Who Guards the Distant Lands, and Yao Nan, General Who Restores Might, against him. Gou Ke defeated them.

sentences.zh: 姚諶討渴，擒之。

translations.literal: Yao Chen campaigned against Ke and seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chen captured Gou Ke in a second expedition.

sentences.zh: 泓使輔國斂曼嵬、前將軍姚光兒討楊倦于陳倉，倦奔于散關。

translations.literal: Hong sent Lian Manwei, General Who Supports the State, and Forward General Yao Guang’er to attack Yang Juan at Chencang. Juan fled to San Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent Lian Manwei, General Who Supports the State, and Forward General Yao Guang’er to attack Yang Juan at Chencang. Juan fled to San Pass.

sentences.zh: 勃勃遣兄子提南侵池陽，車騎姚裕、前將軍彭白狼、建義蛇玄距卻之。

translations.literal: Bobo sent Ti, his elder brother’s son, south to invade Chiyang. Yao Yu, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Forward General Peng Bailang, and General She Xuan, who held the title Jianyi, met his attack and drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: Bobo sent Ti, his elder brother’s son, south to invade Chiyang. Yao Yu, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Forward General Peng Bailang, and General She Xuan, who held the title Jianyi, met his attack and drove him back.

sentences.zh: 尋而晉太尉劉裕總大軍伐泓，次於彭城，遣冠軍將軍檀道濟、龍驤將軍王鎮惡入自淮、肥，攻漆丘、項城，將軍沈林子自汴入河，攻倉垣。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Yu, grand commandant of Jin, led a great army against Hong and halted at Pengcheng. He sent Champion General Tan Daoji and Dragon-Soaring General Wang Zhen'e in by the Huai and Fei rivers to attack Qiqiu and Xiangcheng. General Shen Linzi went from the Bian into the Yellow River to attack Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jin’s grand commandant Liu Yu led a great army against Yao Hong and halted at Pengcheng. He sent Champion General Tan Daoji and Dragon-Soaring General Wang Zhen’e in by the Huai and Fei rivers to attack Qiqiu and Xiangcheng. General Shen Linzi entered the Yellow River from the Bian and attacked Cangyuan.

sentences.zh: 泓將王苟生以漆丘降鎮惡，徐州刺史姚掌以項城降道濟，王師遂入潁口，所至多降服。

translations.literal: Hong’s general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Wang Zhen’e, and Yao Zhang, inspector of Xuzhou, surrendered Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji. The Jin army then entered Yingkou, and many places submitted as it advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Hong’s general Wang Gousheng surrendered Qiqiu to Wang Zhen’e, and Yao Zhang, inspector of Xuzhou, surrendered Xiangcheng to Tan Daoji. The Jin army then entered Yingkou, and many places submitted as it advanced.

sentences.zh: 惟新蔡太守董遵固守不降，道濟攻破之，縛遵而致諸軍門。

translations.literal: Only Xin'cai Grand Administrator Dong Zun firmly guarded and would not surrender; Daoji broke him, bound Zun, and brought him to the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Only Dong Zun, governor of Xincai, held firm and refused to surrender. Tan Daoji stormed the place, had Zun bound and brought him to the gate of the camp.

sentences.zh: 遵厲色曰：「古之王者伐國，待士以禮。

translations.literal: With a stern expression Dong Zun said, “When kings of old made war on other states, they treated men of worth with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: With a stern expression Dong Zun said, “When kings of old made war on other states, they treated men of worth with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 君奈何以不義行師，待國土以非禮乎。」

translations.literal: How can you wage war unjustly and treat a man of distinction in another state with such discourtesy?”
translations.idiomatic: How can you wage war unjustly and treat a man of distinction in another state with such discourtesy?”

sentences.zh: 道濟怒殺之。

translations.literal: Daoji in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji killed him in fury.

sentences.zh: 姚紹聞王師之至，還長安，言於泓曰：「晉師已過許昌，豫州、安定孤遠，卒難救衛，宜遷諸鎮戶內實京畿，可得精兵十萬，足以橫行天下。

translations.literal: When Yao Shao heard the royal army had arrived, he returned to Chang'an and said to Hong, "The Jin army has passed Xuchang; Yuzhou and Anding are isolated and far; in the end hard to rescue—it is fitting to move the garrison households inward to fill the capital region; you can obtain crack troops of one hundred thousand, enough to range across the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the Jin army had arrived, Yao Shao returned to Chang’an and told Hong, “Jin has already passed Xuchang. Yuzhou and Anding are isolated and distant. It would be hard to relieve them at short notice. Move the garrison households inward to strengthen the capital region. We could raise a hundred thousand picked troops, enough to range unchallenged throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 假使二寇交侵，無深害也。

translations.literal: Even if the two bandits jointly invade, there is no deep harm.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Bobo and Jin strike together, a thick core can absorb the blow.

sentences.zh: 如其不爾，晉侵豫州，勃勃寇安定者，將若之何！

translations.literal: If it is not so—Jin invading Yuzhou and Bobo raiding Anding—what is to be done!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise Jin will chew Yuzhou while Bobo gnaws Anding—what then?

sentences.zh: 事機已至，宜在速決。」

translations.literal: The moment of affairs has arrived; it is fitting to decide with speed."
translations.idiomatic: The hour demands a fast decision."

sentences.zh: 其左僕射梁喜曰：「齊公恢雄勇有威名，為嶺北所憚，鎮人已與勃勃深仇，理應守死無貳，勃勃終不能棄安定遠寇京畿。

translations.literal: His left vice-director Liang Xi said, "Duke of Qi Hui is fierce and brave and has an awesome name, feared north of the ridge; the garrison people already have deep hatred with Bobo, by principle ought to guard unto death without second mind—Bobo in the end cannot abandon Anding and raid the capital region far.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi, the left vice-director, said, “Yao Hui, Duke of Qi, is brave and has a formidable reputation. The people north of the ridge fear him. The garrison’s people already bear Bobo a deep grudge and should hold out to the death without wavering. Bobo cannot bypass Anding and raid the distant capital region.

sentences.zh: 若無安定，虜馬必及於郿、雍。

translations.literal: If there is no Anding, enemy horses will surely reach Mei and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Lose Anding and enemy horsemen will reach Mei and Yong.

sentences.zh: 今關中兵馬足距晉師，豈可未有憂危先自削損也。」

translations.literal: Now Guanzhong troops and horses are enough to stop the Jin army—how can one, not yet having worry and peril, first wound oneself by cutting away!"
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong can still face Jin—why cripple yourself before the crisis?"

sentences.zh: 泓從之。

translations.literal: Hong followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sided with Liang Xi.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎懿橫密言於泓曰：「齊公恢于廣平之難有忠勳于陛下，自陛下龍飛紹統，未有殊賞以答其意。

translations.literal: Yi Heng, a gentleman of the Personnel Department, privately told Hong, “Yao Hui, Duke of Qi, rendered Your Majesty loyal service in the crisis over the Duke of Guangping. Since Your Majesty rose like a dragon and succeeded to the throne, no special reward has acknowledged Hui’s devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Heng, a gentleman of the Personnel Department, privately told Hong, “Yao Hui, Duke of Qi, rendered Your Majesty loyal service in the crisis over the Duke of Guangping. Since you took the throne, he has received no special reward in recognition of his devotion.

sentences.zh: 今外則致之死地，內則不豫朝權，安定人自以孤危逼寇，欲思南遷者十室而九，若擁精兵四萬，鼓行而向京師，得不為社稷之累乎！

translations.literal: Now outside he is cast into a dead place, inside he does not share court power; Anding men themselves think isolated and endangered by the raider—those who wish to think of moving south are nine houses in ten—if he rallies crack troops of forty thousand and drums his march toward the capital, could it not be a burden on the altars!
translations.idiomatic: Now outside he is cast into a dead place, and inside he does not share court power; the men of Anding think themselves isolated and pressed by the raider—nine houses in ten wish to move south. If he rallies forty thousand crack troops and drums his march on the capital, would that not burden the altars?

sentences.zh: 宜征還朝廷，以慰其心。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to summon him back to court to comfort his mind."
translations.idiomatic: Recall him to the capital to calm him."

sentences.zh: 泓曰：「恢若懷不逞之心，征之適所以速禍耳。」

translations.literal: Hong said, "If Hui harbors a mind of unfulfilled ambition, summoning him would only hasten disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong said: "If Yao Hui is disloyal, recalling him would only hasten revolt."

sentences.zh: 又不從。

translations.literal: Again he did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: He refused again.

sentences.zh: 王師至成皋，征南姚洸時鎮洛陽，馳使請救。

translations.literal: When the royal army reached Chenggao, General Who Conquers the South Yao Guang then garrisoned Luoyang, sent dispatch riders requesting rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin army reached Chenggao, Yao Guang, General Who Conquers the South, was garrisoning Luoyang. He sent a rider at speed to request relief.

sentences.zh: 泓遣越騎校尉閻生率騎三千以赴之，武衛姚益男將步卒一萬助守洛陽，又遣征東、并州牧姚懿南屯陝津為之聲援。

translations.literal: Hong sent Yan Sheng, colonel of the Yue Cavalry, with three thousand horsemen to the rescue. Martial Guard commander Yao Yinan led ten thousand infantry to help defend Luoyang. Hong also sent Yao Yi, General Who Conquers the East and governor of Bingzhou, south to camp at Shan Ford in support.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent Yan Sheng, colonel of the Yue Cavalry, with three thousand horsemen to the rescue and the Martial Guard commander Yao Yinan with ten thousand infantry to help defend Luoyang. He also sent Yao Yi, General Who Conquers the East and governor of Bingzhou, south to camp at Shan Ford in support.

sentences.zh: 洸部將趙玄說洸曰：「今寇逼已深，百姓駭懼，眾寡勢殊，難以應敵。

translations.literal: Guang's subordinate Zhao Xuan spoke to Guang, saying, "Now the raider's pressure is already deep, the hundred surnames are terrified; few and many, the power situation is unequal—hard to answer the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Guang’s subordinate commander Zhao Xuan urged him, “The invaders have already penetrated deep into our territory. The people are terrified, and our forces are so outnumbered that it will be hard to meet the enemy.

sentences.zh: 宜攝諸戍兵士，固守金墉，以待京師之援，不可出戰。

translations.literal: You ought to gather the garrison soldiers and firmly guard the Metal Rampart, awaiting rescue from the capital region; you must not go out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Pull every defender behind the Metal Rampart and wait for relief from Chang'an—do not offer battle outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 如脫不捷，大事去矣。

translations.literal: If perchance you are not victorious, the great enterprise is gone.
translations.idiomatic: Lose that fight and the cause is lost.

sentences.zh: 金墉既固，師無損敗，吳寇終不敢越金墉而西。

translations.literal: Once Metal Rampart is firm, the army suffers no defeat, and the Wu bandits in the end dare not cross Metal Rampart westward.
translations.idiomatic: With Jinyong strongly held and our army intact, the invaders from Wu will never dare pass the fortress and march west.

sentences.zh: 困之於堅城之下，可以坐制其弊。」

translations.literal: Trap them beneath a strong city; you can sit and control their exhaustion."
translations.idiomatic: Keep them pinned beneath strong walls, and you can wait and take advantage of their exhaustion.”

sentences.zh: 時洸司馬姚禹潛通於道濟，主簿閻恢、楊虔等皆禹之党，嫉玄忠誠，咸共毀之，固勸洸出戰。

translations.literal: At that time Guang's Major Yao Yu secretly communicated with Daoji; chief clerk Yan Hui and Yang Qian and others were all Yu's faction, jealous of Xuan's loyalty, together slandered him, and firmly urged Guang to go out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Guang's Major Yao Yu was in secret communication with Tan Daoji; Chief Clerk Yan Hui, Yang Qian, and others were all Yu's faction, jealous of Zhao Xuan's loyalty; they slandered him together and firmly urged Guang to go out to battle.

sentences.zh: 洸從之，乃遣玄率精兵千餘南守柏穀塢，廣武石無諱東戍鞏城，以距王師。

translations.literal: Guang took their advice and sent Zhao Xuan south with over a thousand picked troops to defend the Baigu stockade, and General Shi Wuhui, holder of the title Guangwu, east to garrison Gongcheng and bar the Jin army.
translations.idiomatic: Guang took their advice and sent Zhao Xuan south with over a thousand picked troops to defend the Baigu stockade, and General Shi Wuhui, holder of the title Guangwu, east to garrison Gongcheng and bar the Jin army.

sentences.zh: 玄泣謂洸曰：「玄受三帝重恩，所守正死耳。

translations.literal: Xuan wept and said to Guang, “Three emperors have shown me great favor. All I can do is die at my post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xuan wept: "Three emperors favored me—I mean to die loyally here.

sentences.zh: 但明公不用忠臣之言，為奸孽所誤，後必悔之，但無及耳。」

translations.literal: But the enlightened lord does not use loyal ministers' words, is misled by evil spawn—later you will regret it, but it will not be in time!"
translations.idiomatic: You spurn loyal counsel for flatterers—you will regret this when it is too late!"

sentences.zh: 會陽城及成皋、滎陽、武牢諸城悉降，道濟等長驅而至。

translations.literal: When Yangcheng and Chenggao, Xingyang, Wulao citadels all surrendered, Daoji and others drove straight through.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Yangcheng, Chenggao, Xingyang and Wulao all surrendered, and Tan Daoji and the others advanced swiftly without a check.

sentences.zh: 無諱至石關，奔還。

translations.literal: Wuhui reached Stone Pass and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wuhui reached Stone Pass and fled back.

sentences.zh: 玄與晉將毛德祖戰于柏穀，以眾寡而敗，被瘡十餘，據地大呼，玄司馬騫鑒冒刃抱玄而泣，玄曰：「吾瘡已重，君宜速去。」

translations.literal: Xuan fought Jin general Mao Dezu at Baigu; because few against many he was defeated, received more than ten wounds, clutched the ground and shouted; Xuan's Major Qian Jian braved blades, embraced Xuan and wept; Xuan said, "My wounds are already heavy—you ought quickly to depart."
translations.idiomatic: At Baigu, Zhao Xuan fought the Jin general Mao Dezu and was defeated by superior numbers. He received more than ten wounds and cried out from the ground. His major, Qian Jian, braved the blades to hold him in his arms and wept. Xuan said, “My wounds are grave. You must leave at once.”

sentences.zh: 鑒曰：「若將軍不濟，當與俱死，去將安之！」

translations.literal: Qian said, "If the general does not succeed, I should die with you—where would I go leaving!"
translations.idiomatic: Qian Jian replied, “If you do not survive, General, I will die with you. If I left, where would I go?”

sentences.zh: 皆死於陣。

translations.literal: Both died in the formation.
translations.idiomatic: Both died on the field.

sentences.zh: 姚禹逾城奔于王師。

translations.literal: Yao Yu climbed the wall and fled to the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yu went over the wall to Jin.

sentences.zh: 道濟進至洛陽、洸懼，遂降。

translations.literal: Daoji advanced to Luoyang; Guang feared and then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji reached Luoyang; Yao Guang surrendered in panic.

sentences.zh: 時閻生至新安，益男至湖城，會洛陽已沒，遂留屯不進。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Sheng had reached Xin'an, Yinan had reached Hucheng; when Luoyang had already fallen, they therefore halted and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Sheng had reached Xin’an and Yao Yinan had reached Hucheng. Luoyang had already fallen, so they stayed in camp and advanced no farther.

sentences.zh: 姚懿嶮薄，惑於信受，其司馬孫暢奸巧傾佞，好亂樂禍，勸懿襲長安，誅姚紹，廢泓自立。

translations.literal: Yao Yi was perilous and mean, deluded by what he trusted; his Major Sun Chang was crafty, fawning, fond of turmoil and rejoicing in disaster, urging Yi to raid Chang'an, kill Yao Shao, depose Hong and set himself up.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi was mean and treacherous and easily misled by those he trusted. His major Sun Chang, a cunning flatterer who delighted in turmoil and misfortune, urged him to raid Chang’an, kill Yao Shao, depose Yao Hong and set himself on the throne.

sentences.zh: 懿納之，乃引兵至陝津，散谷以賜河北夷夏，欲虛損國儲，招引和戎諸羌，樹已私惠。

translations.literal: Yi took his advice and led troops to Shan Ford. He distributed grain to the non-Chinese and Chinese inhabitants north of the Yellow River, intending to deplete the state reserves, attract the Qiang groups of Herong and win personal credit for the largesse.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took his advice and led troops to Shan Ford. He distributed grain to the non-Chinese and Chinese inhabitants north of the Yellow River, intending to deplete the state reserves, attract the Qiang groups of Herong and win personal credit for the largesse.

sentences.zh: 懿左常侍張敞、侍郎左雅固諫懿曰：「殿下以母弟之親，居分陝之重，安危休戚，與國共之。

translations.literal: Yi’s Left Regular Attendant Zhang Chang and Attendant Gentleman Zuo Ya earnestly remonstrated with him: “Your Highness is the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother. You bear the weight of regional command and share the state’s safety and danger, its joys and its sorrows.
translations.idiomatic: Yi’s Left Regular Attendant Zhang Chang and Attendant Gentleman Zuo Ya earnestly remonstrated with him: “Your Highness is the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother. You bear the weight of regional command and share the state’s safety and danger, its joys and its sorrows.

sentences.zh: 漢有七國之難，實賴梁王。

translations.literal: Han had the disaster of the seven states—it truly relied on the Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Han survived the Seven Kingdoms revolt because the Prince of Liang stood firm.

sentences.zh: 今吳寇內侵，四州傾沒，西虜擾邊，秦、涼覆敗，朝廷之危有同累卵，正是諸侯勤王之日。

translations.literal: Now the Wu bandit invades within, four provinces have toppled, western raiders disturb the border, Qin and Liang are overthrown—the court's peril is like piled eggs; this is exactly the day when lords should aid the king.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu invaders are now inside, four provinces have fallen, western raiders disturb the border, and Qin and Liang have been overthrown—the court's peril is like piled eggs; this is the hour for the lords to rally to the throne.

sentences.zh: 谷者，國之本也，而今散之。

translations.literal: Grain is the state's root, yet now you scatter it.
translations.idiomatic: Grain is the foundation of the state, yet you are giving it away.

sentences.zh: 若朝廷問殿下者，將何辭以報？」

translations.literal: If the court asks Your Highness, with what words will you answer?"
translations.idiomatic: If the court questions Your Highness, what will you say in reply?”

sentences.zh: 懿怒，笞而殺之。

translations.literal: Yi in anger flogged and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: In anger, Yao Yi had the two men flogged and killed.

sentences.zh: 泓聞之，召姚紹等密謀於朝堂。

translations.literal: When Hong heard it, he summoned Yao Shao and others to plot secretly in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Hong heard of this, he summoned Yao Shao and others to deliberate in secret in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「懿性識鄙近，從物推移，造成此事，惟當孫暢耳。

translations.literal: Shao said, "Yi's nature and insight are base and near, following things as they shift; what made this affair is only Sun Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao said, “Yi is narrow in outlook and easily swayed by others. Sun Chang must be the one behind this affair.

sentences.zh: 但馳使征暢，遣撫軍贊據陝城，臣向潼關為諸軍節度，若暢奉詔而至者，臣當遣懿率河東見兵共平吳寇。

translations.literal: Just send a swift rider to summon Sun Chang, and send Pacifying General Yao Zan to hold the city of Shan. I will go to Tong Pass to direct the armies. If Chang comes in obedience to the edict, I will have Yi lead the troops now available in Hedong to join us against the invaders from Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Just send a swift rider to summon Sun Chang, and send Pacifying General Yao Zan to hold the city of Shan. I will go to Tong Pass to direct the armies. If Chang comes in obedience to the edict, I will have Yi lead the troops now available in Hedong to join us against the invaders from Wu.

sentences.zh: 如其逆釁已成，違距詔敕者，當明其罪於天下，聲鼓以擊之。」

translations.literal: If their rebellious rift is already formed and they defy the edict, then make their crime clear to the realm and beat the drums to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: If rebellion is already under way and they resist the edict, we should proclaim their crime to the realm and sound the drums to attack them.”

sentences.zh: 泓曰：「叔父之言，社稷之計也。」

translations.literal: Hong said, "Uncle's words are the plan for the altars."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong said, "Uncle, your plan saves the state."

sentences.zh: 於是遣姚贊及冠軍司馬國璠、建義蛇玄屯陝津，武衛姚驢屯潼關。

translations.literal: Hong sent Yao Zan, Champion General Sima Guofan and General She Xuan, holder of the title Jianyi, to encamp at Shan Ford, and Martial Guard commander Yao Lü to encamp at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent Yao Zan, Champion General Sima Guofan and General She Xuan, holder of the title Jianyi, to encamp at Shan Ford, and Martial Guard commander Yao Lü to encamp at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 懿遂舉兵僭號，傳檄州郡，欲運匈奴堡穀以給鎮人。

translations.literal: Yi thereupon raised troops and presumptuously assumed title, circulated call to arms to province and commandery, wished to transport Xiongnu Fort grain to supply the garrison men.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yi raised troops, claimed the sovereign title and circulated proclamations to the provinces and commanderies. He sought to move grain from the Xiongnu fort to provision the garrison.

sentences.zh: 甯東姚成都距之，懿乃卑辭招誘，深自結托，送佩刀為誓，成都送以呈泓。

translations.literal: General Who Calms the East Yao Chengdu blocked him; Yi then used humble words to entice and win him, deeply pledged himself, sent a belt knife as oath—Chengdu sent it to present to Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chengdu, General Who Pacifies the East, resisted him. Yi tried to win Chengdu over with humble words and bind him closely to himself, sending his belt knife as a pledge. Chengdu sent the knife on to Hong.

sentences.zh: 懿又遣驍騎王國率甲士數百攻成都，成都擒國，囚之，遣讓懿曰：「明公以母弟之親，受推轂之寄，今社稷之危若綴旒然，宜恭恪憂勤，匡輔王室。

translations.literal: Yi then sent the Valiant Cavalry commander Wang Guo with several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu. Chengdu captured and imprisoned Guo and sent Yi this rebuke: “As the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother, you were entrusted with military command. The state now hangs as precariously as a dangling tassel. You ought to serve with reverent care and diligence and uphold the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Yi then sent the Valiant Cavalry commander Wang Guo with several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu. Chengdu captured and imprisoned Guo and sent Yi this rebuke: “As the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother, you were entrusted with military command. The state now hangs as precariously as a dangling tassel. You ought to serve with reverent care and diligence and uphold the royal house.

sentences.zh: 而更包藏奸宄，謀危宗廟，三祖之靈豈安公乎！

translations.literal: Yet you harbor treachery and plot danger to the ancestral temple—can the spirits of the three ancestors rest easy with you!
translations.idiomatic: Instead you harbor treachery and plot to endanger the dynasty. How could the spirits of our three ancestors rest easy over your conduct?

sentences.zh: 此鎮之糧，一方所寄，鎮人何功，而欲給之！

translations.literal: This garrison's grain is what one region relies on—what merit have garrison men that you wish to supply them!
translations.idiomatic: This garrison’s grain is the support of the whole region. What merit have your garrison men shown that you would give it to them?

sentences.zh: 王國為蛇畫足，國之罪人，已就囚執，聽詔而戮之。

translations.literal: Wang Guo added feet to a snake. He is a criminal against the state and is already in custody. I await the imperial order to put him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guo has made matters worse by his needless intervention, like someone drawing feet on a snake. He is a criminal against the state and is already in custody. I await the imperial order to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 成都方糾合義眾，以懲明公之罪，復須大兵悉集，當與明公會於河上。」

translations.literal: Chengdu is now gathering righteous hosts to punish the enlightened lord's crime; again must great hosts all assemble—I will meet the enlightened lord on the river.
translations.idiomatic: I am now rallying loyal men to punish your crime. When the whole army has assembled, I will meet you on the Yellow River.”

sentences.zh: 乃宣告諸城，勉以忠義，厲兵秣馬，徵發義租。

translations.literal: Chengdu sent proclamations to the cities, exhorting them to loyalty and righteousness. He sharpened weapons, fed the horses and levied contributions for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu sent proclamations to the cities, exhorting them to loyalty and righteousness. He sharpened weapons, fed the horses and levied contributions for the cause.

sentences.zh: 河東之兵無詣懿者，懿深患之。

translations.literal: Not one Hedong soldier went to Yi; Yi deeply worried over it.
translations.idiomatic: No troops from Hedong went over to Yao Yi, and this worried him deeply.

sentences.zh: 臨晉數千戶叛應懿。

translations.literal: Several thousand households of Linjin rebelled to answer Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand households in Linjin rose in support of Yao Yi.

sentences.zh: 姚紹濟自薄津，擊臨晉叛戶，大破之，懿等震懼。

translations.literal: Yao Shao crossed from Bo ford, struck the Linjin rebel households, greatly defeated them; Yi and others were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao crossed at Bo Ford and routed the rebel households of Linjin. Yao Yi and his followers were shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 鎮人安定郭純、王奴等率眾圍懿。

translations.literal: Garrison men of Anding Guo Chun and Wang Nu and others led hosts to surround Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chun, Wang Nu and other garrison men from Anding led their followers in surrounding Yao Yi.

sentences.zh: 紹入于蒲阪，執懿囚之，誅孫暢等。

translations.literal: Shao entered Puban, seized Yi and imprisoned him, executed Sun Chang and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao entered Puban, captured and imprisoned Yao Yi, and executed Sun Chang and others.

sentences.zh: 泓以內外離叛，王師漸逼，歲旦朝群臣於其前殿，淒然流涕，群臣皆泣。

translations.literal: Because inner and outer split in rebellion and the royal army pressed gradually, on New Year's dawn Hong met the host of ministers in his front hall, wept dismally; the host of ministers all wept.
translations.idiomatic: With defections at home and abroad and the Jin army drawing nearer, Yao Hong received his ministers in the front hall on New Year’s morning. He shed tears of grief, and the ministers all wept.

sentences.zh: 時征北姚恢率安定鎮戶三萬八千，焚燒室宇，以車為方陣，自北雍州趣長安，自稱大都督、建義大將軍，移檄州郡，欲除君側之惡。

translations.literal: At the time General Who Conquers the North Yao Hui led thirty-eight thousand Anding garrison households, burned houses, formed a chariot square, went from North Yongzhou toward Chang'an, styled himself grand commander-in-chief and great general who establishes righteousness, circulated call to arms to province and commandery, wishing to remove evil beside the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hui, General Who Conquers the North, burned the houses and led thirty-eight thousand Anding garrison households toward Chang’an from North Yongzhou, forming his wagons into a square. He styled himself grand commander-in-chief and Great General Who Establishes Righteousness and sent proclamations to the provinces and commanderies declaring his intent to rid the ruler’s side of evil men.

sentences.zh: 揚威姜紀率眾奔之。

translations.literal: General Who Displays Might Jiang Ji led hosts to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Ji, General Who Displays Might, led his men to join Hui.

sentences.zh: 建節彭完都聞恢將至，棄陰密，奔還長安。

translations.literal: When General Peng Wandu, holder of the title Jianjie, heard that Hui was approaching, he abandoned Yinmi and fled back to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: When General Peng Wandu, holder of the title Jianjie, heard that Hui was approaching, he abandoned Yinmi and fled back to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 恢至新支，姜紀說恢曰：「國家重將在東，京師空虛，公可輕兵徑襲，事必克矣。」

translations.literal: When Hui reached Xin-zhi, Jiang Ji urged Hui, saying, "The state's weighty generals are in the east; the capital is empty—with light troops you could raid straight in; the affair would surely succeed."
translations.idiomatic: When Hui reached Xinzhi, Jiang Ji urged him, “The state’s leading generals are in the east, leaving the capital undefended. If you strike straight at it with light troops, you are sure to succeed.”

sentences.zh: 恢不從，乃南攻郿城。

translations.literal: Hui did not follow, then attacked south toward Mei city.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hui refused and struck south for Mei instead.

sentences.zh: 鎮西姚諶為恢所敗，恢軍勢彌盛，長安大震。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the West Yao Chen was defeated by Hui; Hui's army momentum grew ever stronger; Chang'an was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hui defeated Yao Chen, General Who Guards the West. Hui’s army gathered still greater strength, and Chang’an was badly shaken.

sentences.zh: 泓馳使征紹，遣姚裕及輔國胡翼度屯於灃西。

translations.literal: Hong dispatched riders summoning Shao, sent Yao Yu and General Who Supports the State Hu Yidu to camp west of the Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent a rider at speed to summon Yao Shao and ordered Yao Yu and Hu Yidu, General Who Supports the State, to camp west of the Feng River.

sentences.zh: 扶風太守姚雋、安夷護軍姚墨蠡、建威姚娥都、揚威彭蠔皆懼而降恢。

translations.literal: Yao Jun, governor of Fufeng, Yao Moli, army protector at Anyi, Yao E’du, General Who Establishes Might, and Peng Hao, General Who Displays Might, all surrendered to Hui out of fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Jun, governor of Fufeng, Yao Moli, army protector at Anyi, Yao E’du, General Who Establishes Might, and Peng Hao, General Who Displays Might, all surrendered to Hui out of fear.

sentences.zh: 恢舅苟和時為立節將軍，守忠不貳，泓召而謂之曰：「眾人咸懷去就，卿何能自安邪？」

translations.literal: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He, then a general with the title Lijie, remained unswervingly loyal. Hong summoned him and asked, “Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay. How can you remain at ease?”
translations.idiomatic: Hui’s maternal uncle Gou He, then a general with the title Lijie, remained unswervingly loyal. Hong summoned him and asked, “Everyone is weighing whether to leave or stay. How can you remain at ease?”

sentences.zh: 和曰：「若天縱妖賊，得肆其逆節者，舅甥之理，不待賓士而加親。

translations.literal: Gou He replied, “If Heaven lets this wicked rebel have his way and carry through his revolt, our bond as uncle and nephew needs no rushing to his side to make it closer.
translations.idiomatic: Gou He replied, “If Heaven lets this wicked rebel have his way and carry through his revolt, our bond as uncle and nephew needs no rushing to his side to make it closer.

sentences.zh: 如其罪極逆銷，天盈其罰者，守忠執志，臣之體也。

translations.literal: If his crime reaches its limit and treason melts, Heaven filling his punishment, keeping loyalty and holding resolve—that is the body of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: If instead his crimes reach their limit, his rebellion comes to nothing and Heaven visits its full punishment on him, my duty as a subject is to remain loyal and hold to my resolve.

sentences.zh: 違親叛君，臣之所恥。」

translations.literal: To violate kin and betray the lord is what a subject shames.
translations.idiomatic: To turn against my kin or betray my ruler would shame me.”

sentences.zh: 泓善其忠恕，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: Hong praised his loyal forgiveness and added gold seal and purple ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: Hong commended his loyalty and consideration and awarded him a gold seal with a purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 姚紹率輕騎先赴難，使姚洽、司馬國璠將步卒三萬赴長安。

translations.literal: Yao Shao led light cavalry ahead to meet the emergency and sent Yao Qia and Sima Guofan with thirty thousand infantry to hurry to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao led light cavalry ahead to meet the emergency and sent Yao Qia and Sima Guofan with thirty thousand infantry to hurry to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 恢從曲牢進屯杜成，紹與恢相持於靈台。

translations.literal: Hui advanced from Qulao and camped at Ducheng; Shao and Hui faced each other at Lingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hui advanced from Qulao and camped at Ducheng. He and Yao Shao faced one another at Lingtai.

sentences.zh: 姚贊聞恢漸逼，留甯朔尹雅為弘農太守，守潼關，率諸軍還長安。

translations.literal: Hearing that Hui was drawing near, Yao Zan left General Yin Ya, holder of the Ningshuo title, as governor of Hongnong to guard Tong Pass and led the armies back to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Hui was drawing near, Yao Zan left General Yin Ya, holder of the Ningshuo title, as governor of Hongnong to guard Tong Pass and led the armies back to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 泓謝贊曰：「元子不能崇明德義，導率群下，致禍起蕭牆，變自同氣，既上負祖宗，亦無顏見諸父。

translations.literal: Hong acknowledged his fault to Zan: “I, Yuanzi, have failed to uphold and make known the way of virtue and righteousness or to lead my subordinates. I have let disaster arise within my walls and rebellion break out among my own brothers. I have failed my ancestors and am ashamed to face my uncles.
translations.idiomatic: Hong acknowledged his fault to Zan: “I, Yuanzi, have failed to uphold and make known the way of virtue and righteousness or to lead my subordinates. I have let disaster arise within my walls and rebellion break out among my own brothers. I have failed my ancestors and am ashamed to face my uncles.

sentences.zh: 懿始構逆滅亡，恢復擁眾內叛，將若之何？」

translations.literal: Yi first plotted rebellion and perished; Hui again embraces hosts in inner rebellion—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi first plotted rebellion and was crushed; Hui again leads hosts in inner revolt—what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 贊曰：「懿等所以敢稱兵內侮者，諒由臣等輕弱，無防遏之方故也。」

translations.literal: Zan said, "The reason Yi and others dared raise arms in inner insult is surely because we ministers are weak and light, without means to prevent and block."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan replied, “Yi and the others dared take up arms and attack us from within surely because we, your ministers, are weak and had no means of forestalling or checking them.”

sentences.zh: 因攘袂大泣曰：「臣與大將軍不滅此賊，終不持面復見陛下！」

translations.literal: Pushing up his sleeves and weeping aloud, Zan said, “Unless the grand general and I destroy this rebel, I will never again show my face before Your Majesty!”
translations.idiomatic: Pushing up his sleeves and weeping aloud, Zan said, “Unless the grand general and I destroy this rebel, I will never again show my face before Your Majesty!”

sentences.zh: 泓於是班賜軍士而遣之。

translations.literal: Hong thereupon distributed gifts to the army soldiers and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong distributed gifts to the soldiers and sent them off.

sentences.zh: 恢眾見諸軍悉集，咸懼而思善，其將齊黃等棄恢而降。

translations.literal: Hui's host seeing all armies assembled all feared and thought of good; his generals Qi Huang and others abandoned Hui and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui’s men saw that the armies had all assembled, fear seized them and they began to think of returning to allegiance. His general Qi Huang and others abandoned him and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 恢進軍逼紹，贊自後要擊，大破之，殺恢及其三弟。

translations.literal: Hui advanced the army pressing Shao; Zan struck him from the rear, greatly defeated him, killed Hui and his three younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: As Hui advanced against Shao, Zan intercepted him from the rear and routed him, killing Hui and his three younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 泓哭之悲慟，葬以公禮。

translations.literal: Hong wept for him with extreme grief and buried him with ducal rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong wept bitterly for Hui and buried him with the rites of a duke.

sentences.zh: 至是，王鎮惡至宜陽。

translations.literal: By this time Wang Zhen'e had reached Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e had reached Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 毛德祖攻弘農太守尹雅于蠡城，眾潰，德祖使騎追獲之，既而殺晉守者奔固潼關。

translations.literal: Mao Dezu attacked Yin Ya, governor of Hongnong, at Li city. Ya’s troops broke, and Dezu sent cavalry in pursuit and captured him. Later Ya killed his Jin guards and fled to hold Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Dezu attacked Hongnong Grand Administrator Yin Ya at Li city; the host broke and Dezu's cavalry seized him; afterward Yin Ya killed the Jin guards and fled to hold Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 檀道濟、沈林子攻拔襄邑堡，建威薛帛奔河東。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi stormed Xiangyi stockade. Xue Bo, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji and Shen Linzi stormed Xiangyi stockade. Xue Bo, General Who Establishes Might, fled to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 道濟白陝北渡，攻蒲阪，使將軍苟卓攻匈奴堡，為泓甯東姚成都所敗。

translations.literal: Tan Daoji crossed north from Shan to attack Puban and sent General Gou Zhuo to attack Xiongnu Fort. Hong’s General Who Pacifies the East, Yao Chengdu, defeated Gou Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji crossed north from Shan to attack Puban and sent General Gou Zhuo to attack Xiongnu Fort. Hong’s General Who Pacifies the East, Yao Chengdu, defeated Gou Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 泓遣姚驢救蒲阪，胡翼度據潼關。

translations.literal: Hong sent Yao Lü to rescue Puban; Hu Yidu held Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent Yao Lü to relieve Puban, while Hu Yidu held Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 泓進紹太宰、大將軍、大都督、都督中外諸軍事、假黃鋮，改封魯公，侍中、司隸、宗正、節錄並如故，朝之大政皆往決焉。

translations.literal: Hong promoted Shao to grand minister, grand general, grand commander-in-chief and commander of all military affairs at court and in the provinces. He granted him the yellow axe and changed his fief to the dukedom of Lu. Shao retained his offices as palace attendant, metropolitan inspector and director of the imperial clan, his staff of authority and his oversight of the Secretariat. All major matters of court policy went to him for decision.
translations.idiomatic: Hong promoted Shao to grand minister, grand general, grand commander-in-chief and commander of all military affairs at court and in the provinces. He granted him the yellow axe and changed his fief to the dukedom of Lu. Shao retained his offices as palace attendant, metropolitan inspector and director of the imperial clan, his staff of authority and his oversight of the Secretariat. All major matters of court policy went to him for decision.

sentences.zh: 紹固辭，弗許。

translations.literal: Shao firmly declined; he was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao refused the honors; Yao Hong insisted.

sentences.zh: 於是遣紹率武衛姚鸞等步騎五萬，距王師於潼關。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Shao leading Martial Guard Yao Luan and others, fifty thousand foot and horse, to block the royal army at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent Yao Shao, with Martial Guard commander Yao Luan and others, at the head of fifty thousand infantry and cavalry to oppose the Jin army at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 姚驢與并州刺史尹昭為表裏之勢，夾攻道濟。

translations.literal: Yao Lü and Bingzhou Inspector Yin Zhao formed inner-outer posture and jointly attacked Daoji.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Lü and Yin Zhao, inspector of Bingzhou, coordinated their forces inside and outside the defenses and attacked Tan Daoji from both sides.

sentences.zh: 道濟深壁不戰，沈林子說道濟曰：「今蒲阪城堅池浚，非可卒克，攻之傷眾，守之引日，不如棄之，先事潼關。

translations.literal: Daoji kept deep walls and did not fight; Shen Linzi persuaded Daoji, saying, "Now Puban city is firm and moat deep—not to be taken in haste; attacking it wounds the host, guarding it draws out days—better to abandon it and first strike Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji stayed behind his fortifications and declined battle. Shen Linzi urged him, “Puban’s walls are strong and its moat is deep. We cannot take it quickly. An assault would cost us men, and waiting here would waste days. Better abandon it and turn first to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 潼關天限，形勝之地，鎮惡孤軍，勢危力寡，若使姚紹據之，則難圖矣。

translations.literal: Tong Pass is Heaven's barrier, a place of terrain's advantage; Zhen'e is an isolated army, situation perilous and force small—if you let Yao Shao hold it, it will be hard to plan.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Pass is Heaven's barrier, a place of advantageous terrain; Zhen'e is an isolated army, his situation perilous and his force small—if Yao Shao is allowed to hold it, he will be hard to deal with.

sentences.zh: 如克潼關，紹可不戰而服。」

translations.literal: If you take Tong Pass, Shao can be subdued without battle."
translations.idiomatic: Seize the pass and Yao Shao will submit without fighting."

sentences.zh: 道濟從之，乃棄蒲阪，南向潼關。

translations.literal: Daoji followed it, then abandoned Puban and went south toward Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji followed his advice, abandoned Puban and headed south toward Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 姚贊率禁兵七千，自渭北而東，進據蒲津。

translations.literal: Yao Zan led seven thousand household troops from north of the Wei eastward and advanced to occupy Pu ford.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan led seven thousand palace guards east from north of the Wei River and advanced to occupy Pu Ford.

sentences.zh: 劉裕使沈田子及傅弘之率眾萬餘人入上洛，所在多委城鎮奔長安。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi leading more than ten thousand to enter Shangluo; place after place mostly abandoned cities and towns and fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Shen Tianzi and Fu Hongzhi into Shangluo with more than ten thousand men. In many places people abandoned their cities and garrisons and fled to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 田子等進及青泥，姚紹方陣而前，以距道濟。

translations.literal: Tianzi and others advanced as far as Qingni; Yao Shao formed square array and advanced to block Daoji.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tianzi and the others advanced as far as Qingni, while Yao Shao advanced in square formation to bar Tan Daoji’s way.

sentences.zh: 道濟固壘不戰，紹乃攻其西營，不克，遂以大眾逼之。

translations.literal: Daoji kept firm ramparts and did not fight; Shao then attacked his western camp, did not take it, then pressed with the great host.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji stayed behind walls; Yao Shao stormed his west camp, failed, then massed against him.

sentences.zh: 道濟率王敬、沈林子等逆沖紹軍，將士驚散，引還定城。

translations.literal: Daoji led Wang Jing, Shen Linzi and others in a charge against Shao’s army. Shao’s officers and men scattered in alarm and fell back to Dingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji led Wang Jing, Shen Linzi, and others in a straight charge at Shao's army; Shao's officers and soldiers were startled and scattered and drew back to Dingcheng.

sentences.zh: 紹留姚鸞守險，絕道濟糧道。

translations.literal: Shao left Yao Luan guarding the narrows, cutting Daoji's grain road.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao left Yao Luan to hold the narrows and cut Tan Daoji’s grain route.

sentences.zh: 時裕別將姚珍入自子午，竇霸入自洛穀，眾各數千人。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Yu's separate general Yao Zhen entered from Ziwu, Dou Ba entered from Luogu, each several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu’s detachment commanders Yao Zhen and Dou Ba led separate forces of several thousand men each, Yao Zhen entering by Ziwu and Dou Ba by Luogu.

sentences.zh: 泓遣姚萬距霸，姚彊距珍。

translations.literal: Hong sent Yao Wan to block Ba, Yao Qiang to block Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Yao Wan to oppose Dou Ba and Yao Qiang to oppose Yao Zhen.

sentences.zh: 姚鸞遣將尹雅與道濟司馬徐琰于潼關南，為琰所獲，送之劉裕。

translations.literal: Yao Luan sent general Yin Ya against Daoji's major Xu Yan south of Tong Pass; Ya was seized by Yan and sent to Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Luan sent his general Yin Ya against Xu Yan, Tan Daoji’s major, south of Tong Pass. Xu Yan captured Yin Ya and sent him to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕以雅前叛，欲殺之。

translations.literal: Yu because Ya had formerly rebelled, wished to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu meant to execute Yin Ya for past treason.

sentences.zh: 雅曰：「前活本在望外，今死寧不甘心。

translations.literal: Yin Ya said, “Surviving the first time was already more than I had hoped for. How could I be unwilling to die now?
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ya said, “Surviving the first time was already more than I had hoped for. How could I be unwilling to die now?

sentences.zh: 明公將以大義平天下，豈可使秦無守信之臣乎！」

translations.literal: The enlightened lord will use great righteousness to pacify the realm—how can you make Qin lack a faithful subject!"
translations.idiomatic: You intend to pacify the realm through great righteousness. How can you deny Qin a minister who keeps faith with his ruler?”

sentences.zh: 裕嘉而免之。

translations.literal: Yu praised him and spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu admired him and let him live.

sentences.zh: 泓遣給事黃門侍郎姚和都屯于堯柳，以備田子。

translations.literal: Hong sent Yao Hedu, an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gates, to encamp at Yaoliu as a precaution against Shen Tianzi.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent Yao Hedu, an attendant gentleman of the Yellow Gates, to encamp at Yaoliu as a precaution against Shen Tianzi.

sentences.zh: 姚紹謂諸將曰：「道濟等遠來送死，眾旅不多，嬰壘自固者，正欲曠日持久，以待繼援耳。

translations.literal: Yao Shao told his generals, “Daoji and the others have come a long way to their deaths. Their forces are small. They cling to their ramparts to defend themselves only because they want to gain time until reinforcements arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao told his generals, “Daoji and the others have come a long way to their deaths. Their forces are small. They cling to their ramparts to defend themselves only because they want to gain time until reinforcements arrive.

sentences.zh: 吾欲分軍還據閿鄉，以絕其糧運，不至一月，道濟之首可懸之麾下矣。

translations.literal: I wish to divide the army and return to hold Wenxiang to cut their grain transport—within not one month, Daoji's head can hang beneath the banner.
translations.idiomatic: I want to send part of our army back to hold Wenxiang and cut their grain transport. Before a month has passed, Daoji’s head can hang beneath my standard.

sentences.zh: 濟等既沒，裕計自沮。」

translations.literal: Once Ji and others are gone, Yu's plan will naturally be blocked."
translations.idiomatic: Once Daoji and the others are destroyed, Liu Yu’s plans will come to nothing.”

sentences.zh: 諸將咸以為然。

translations.literal: All generals all thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: The generals agreed.

sentences.zh: 其將胡翼度曰：「軍勢宜集不可以分，若偏師不利，人心駭懼，胡可以戰！」

translations.literal: His general Hu Yidu said, "Army momentum ought to be gathered and cannot be divided; if a partial army is not successful, human hearts will be terrified with alarm—how then can we fight!"
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yidu, one of Shao’s generals, said, “We must concentrate our forces and keep them together. If a detachment suffers a reverse, the men will be seized with fear. How could we fight then?”

sentences.zh: 紹乃止。

translations.literal: Shao then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao dropped his plan to split the army.

sentences.zh: 薛帛據河曲以叛。

translations.literal: Xue Bo occupied the river bend in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bo rebelled from the river bend.

sentences.zh: 紹分道置諸軍為掎角之勢，遣輔國胡翼度據東原，武衛姚鸞營于大路，與晉軍相接。

translations.literal: Shao positioned his armies along separate routes so they could support each other. He sent Hu Yidu, General Who Supports the State, to hold the eastern plain and Martial Guard commander Yao Luan to encamp on the main road, in contact with the Jin army.
translations.idiomatic: Shao positioned his armies along separate routes so they could support each other. He sent Hu Yidu, General Who Supports the State, to hold the eastern plain and Martial Guard commander Yao Luan to encamp on the main road, in contact with the Jin army.

sentences.zh: 沈林子簡精銳銜枚夜襲之，鸞眾潰戰死，士卒死者九千餘人。

translations.literal: Shen Linzi picked elite troops and had them hold gags in their mouths to keep silent during a night attack. Yao Luan’s force broke and he died in battle. More than nine thousand soldiers were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linzi picked elite troops and had them hold gags in their mouths to keep silent during a night attack. Yao Luan’s force broke and he died in battle. More than nine thousand soldiers were killed.

sentences.zh: 姚贊屯於河上，遣恢武姚難運蒲阪穀以給其軍，至香城，為王師所敗。

translations.literal: Yao Zan camped on the river, sent General Who Restores Might Yao Nan to transport Puban grain to supply the army; reaching Xiangcheng, he was defeated by the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan camped on the Yellow River and sent Yao Nan, General Who Restores Might, to bring grain from Puban to supply his army. When Nan reached Xiangcheng, the Jin army defeated him.

sentences.zh: 時泓遣姚諶守堯柳，姚和都討薛帛於河東，聞王師要難，乃兼道赴救，未至而難敗，固破裕裨將于河曲，遂屯蒲阪。

translations.literal: Hong had sent Yao Chen to guard Yaoliu and Yao Hedu to attack Xue Bo in Hedong. When Hedu heard that the Jin army was intercepting Yao Nan, he hurried by forced marches to help. Nan was defeated before Hedu arrived, but Hedu then defeated a subordinate general of Liu Yu’s at the bend of the Yellow River and camped at Puban.
translations.idiomatic: Hong had sent Yao Chen to guard Yaoliu and Yao Hedu to attack Xue Bo in Hedong. When Hedu heard that the Jin army was intercepting Yao Nan, he hurried by forced marches to help. Nan was defeated before Hedu arrived, but Hedu then defeated a subordinate general of Liu Yu’s at the bend of the Yellow River and camped at Puban.

sentences.zh: 姚贊為林子所敗，單馬奔定城。

translations.literal: Yao Zan was defeated by Linzi, alone on horseback fled to Dingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan fled alone to Dingcheng after Shen Linzi routed him.

sentences.zh: 紹遣左長史姚洽及姚墨蠡等率騎三千屯于河北之九原，欲絕道濟諸縣租輸。

translations.literal: Shao sent left chief clerk Yao Qia and Yao Moli and others leading three thousand horse to camp at Jiuyuan north of the He, wishing to cut off Daoji's county rent convoys.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao sent his left chief clerk Yao Qia, Yao Moli and others with three thousand cavalry to camp at Jiuyuan north of the Yellow River. He meant to cut off the tax-grain shipments that the counties were sending Tan Daoji.

sentences.zh: 洽辭曰：「夫小敵之堅，大敵之擒。

translations.literal: Qia declined, saying, "The firmness of a small enemy is the great enemy's catch.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Qia objected, “A small force that stands its ground becomes the captive of a larger enemy.

sentences.zh: 今兵眾單弱，而遠在河外，雖明公神武，然鞭短勢殊，恐無所及。」

translations.literal: Now the troops are few and weak and far beyond the river—though the enlightened lord is divinely martial, yet the whip is short and the power situation unequal—I fear there is no reaching them."
translations.idiomatic: Our troops are few and weak, far away beyond the Yellow River. For all your military prowess, my lord, your whip is short and the forces unequal. I fear you will be unable to reach us.”

sentences.zh: 紹不聽。

translations.literal: Shao did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Shao ignored him.

sentences.zh: 沈林子率眾八千，耍洽於河上，洽戰死，眾皆沒。

translations.literal: Shen Linzi led eight thousand men to intercept Yao Qia on the Yellow River. Qia died in battle and his entire force was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linzi led eight thousand men to intercept Yao Qia on the Yellow River. Qia died in battle and his entire force was lost.

sentences.zh: 紹聞洽等敗，忿恚發病，托姚贊以後事，使姚難屯關西，紹嘔血而死。

translations.literal: When Shao heard Qia and others were defeated, anger and vexation brought illness; he entrusted later affairs to Yao Zan, sent Yao Nan to camp west of the pass; Shao vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Shao learned of the defeat of Yao Qia and the others, his anger brought on an illness. He entrusted affairs to Yao Zan and sent Yao Nan to encamp west of the pass. Shao vomited blood and died.

sentences.zh: 泓以晉師之逼，遣使乞師于魏。

translations.literal: Because the Jin army pressed, Hong sent envoys begging troops from Wei.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jin army pressed closer, Yao Hong sent envoys to Wei to ask for troops.

sentences.zh: 魏遣司徒、南平公拔拔嵩，正直將軍、安平公乙旃眷，進據河內，遊擊將軍王洛生屯於河東，為泓聲援。

translations.literal: Wei sent Baba Song, minister of education and Duke of Nanping, and Yizhan Juan, Upright General and Duke of Anping, to advance and occupy Henei. Raiding General Wang Luosheng camped in Hedong to support Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei sent Baba Song, minister of education and Duke of Nanping, and Yizhan Juan, Upright General and Duke of Anping, to advance and occupy Henei. Raiding General Wang Luosheng camped in Hedong to support Hong.

sentences.zh: 劉裕次於陝城，遣沈林子率精兵萬餘，越山開道，會沈田子等於青泥，將攻堯柳。

translations.literal: Liu Yu halted at Shan city, sent Shen Linzi with more than ten thousand crack troops to cross mountains opening roads, join Shen Tianzi and others at Qingni, planning to attack Yaoliu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu halted at the city of Shan and sent Shen Linzi with more than ten thousand picked troops to open a route across the mountains. They were to join Shen Tianzi and the others at Qingni for an attack on Yaoliu.

sentences.zh: 泓使姚裕率步騎八千距之，泓躬將大眾繼發。

translations.literal: Hong sent Yao Yu with eight thousand foot and horse to block them; Hong personally led the great host to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Yao Yu ahead with eight thousand infantry and cavalry to oppose them. Hong himself led the main army out after him.

sentences.zh: 裕為田子所敗，泓退次於灞上，關中郡縣多潛通于王師。

translations.literal: Shen Tianzi defeated Yao Yu. Hong fell back and camped at Bashang, and many commanderies and counties in Guanzhong entered into secret communication with the Jin army.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tianzi defeated Yao Yu. Hong fell back and camped at Bashang, and many commanderies and counties in Guanzhong entered into secret communication with the Jin army.

sentences.zh: 劉裕至潼關，遣將軍硃超石、徐猗之會薛帛于河北，以攻蒲阪。

translations.literal: Liu Yu reached Tong Pass and sent the generals Zhu Chaoshi and Xu Yizhi to join Xue Bo north of the Yellow River for an attack on Puban.
