translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu reached Tong Pass and sent the generals Zhu Chaoshi and Xu Yizhi to join Xue Bo north of the Yellow River for an attack on Puban.

sentences.zh: 姚贊距裕于關西，姚難屯於香城。

translations.literal: Yao Zan blocked Yu west of the pass; Yao Nan camped at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan opposed Liu Yu west of the pass, and Yao Nan camped at Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 裕遣王鎮惡、王敬自秋社西渡渭，以逼難軍。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent Wang Zhen’e and Wang Jing west from Qiushe to cross the Wei and press Yao Nan’s army.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent Wang Zhen'e and Wang Jing west from Qiushe to cross the Wei, pressing Nan's army.

sentences.zh: 鎮東姚璞及姚和都擊敗猗之等於蒲阪，猗之遇害，超石棄其眾奔於潼關。

translations.literal: Yao Pu, General Who Guards the East, and Yao Hedu defeated Xu Yizhi and the others at Puban. Xu Yizhi was killed, and Zhu Chaoshi abandoned his men and fled to Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Pu, General Who Guards the East, and Yao Hedu defeated Xu Yizhi and the others at Puban. Xu Yizhi was killed, and Zhu Chaoshi abandoned his men and fled to Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 姚贊遣司馬休之及司馬國璠自軹關向河內，引魏軍以躡裕後。

translations.literal: Yao Zan sent Sima Xiuzhi and Sima Guofan from Zhiguan toward Henei, drawing Wei troops to tread on Yu's rear.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan sent Sima Xiuzhi and Sima Guofan from Zhiguan toward Henei, drawing Wei troops to fall on Liu Yu's rear.

sentences.zh: 姚難既為鎮惡所逼，引師而西。

translations.literal: Nan, already pressed by Zhen'e, drew the army westward.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Nan retreated west before Wang Zhen'e.

sentences.zh: 時大霖雨，渭水泛溢，贊等不得北渡。

translations.literal: At the time great rains fell in succession, the Wei overflowed; Zan and others could not cross north.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains sent the Wei River over its banks, and Yao Zan and the others could not cross to the north.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡水陸兼進，追及姚難。

translations.literal: Zhen'e advanced by water and land together, caught up with Yao Nan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen’e advanced by water and by land and overtook Yao Nan.

sentences.zh: 泓自灞上還軍，次於石橋以援之。

translations.literal: Hong returned the army from Bashang, halted at Stone Bridge to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Hong brought his army back from Bashang and halted at Stone Bridge to support Yao Nan.

sentences.zh: 贊退屯鄭城。

translations.literal: Zan drew back to camp at Zheng city.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan withdrew and encamped at the city of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 鎮北姚彊率郡人數千，與姚難陣於涇上，以距鎮惡。

translations.literal: Yao Qiang, General Who Guards the North, led several thousand men of the commandery and formed ranks with Yao Nan on the Jing River to resist Wang Zhen’e.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Qiang, General Who Guards the North, led several thousand men of the commandery and formed ranks with Yao Nan on the Jing River to resist Wang Zhen’e.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡遣毛德祖擊彊，大敗，彊戰死，難遁還長安。

translations.literal: Zhen'e sent Mao Dezu to strike Qiang, greatly defeated him; Qiang died in battle; Nan fled back to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen’e sent Mao Dezu against Yao Qiang. Qiang’s force was routed, and Qiang died in battle. Yao Nan fled back to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 劉裕進據鄭城。

translations.literal: Liu Yu advanced and occupied Zheng city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu took Zheng.

sentences.zh: 泓使姚裕、尚書龐統屯兵宮中，姚洸屯於灃西，尚書姚白瓜徙四軍雜戶入長安，姚丕守渭橋，胡翼度屯石積，姚贊屯霸東，泓軍於逍遙園。

translations.literal: Hong sent Yao Yu and Minister Pang Tong to camp troops in the palace, Yao Guang west of the Feng, Minister Yao Baigua moved four-army miscellaneous households into Chang'an, Yao Pi guarded Wei Bridge, Hu Yidu camped at Stone Accumulation, Yao Zan east of Ba; Hong encamped at Free-Roam Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong sent Yao Yu and the minister Pang Tong to station troops in the palace, Yao Guang to garrison west of Feng, the minister Yao Baigua to move the mixed households of the four armies into Chang'an, Yao Pi to guard the Wei Bridge, Hu Yidu to garrison Shiji, Yao Zan to garrison east of the Ba, while Hong himself encamped at Xiaoyao Garden.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡夾渭進兵，破姚丕於渭橋。

translations.literal: Zhen'e advanced troops on both sides of the Wei, defeated Yao Pi at Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen’e advanced along both banks of the Wei and defeated Yao Pi at Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 泓自逍遙園赴之，逼水地狹，因丕之敗，遂相踐而退。

translations.literal: Hong went from Free-Roam Garden to aid him; pressed by water, ground narrow, because of Pi's defeat, they trampled each other in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong came from Xiaoyao Garden to help Yao Pi. The ground was narrow against the river, and when Pi was defeated the men trampled one another as they retreated.

sentences.zh: 姚諶及前軍姚烈、左衛姚寶安、散騎王帛、建武姚進、揚威姚蠔、尚書右丞孫玄等皆死於陣，泓單馬還宮。

translations.literal: Yao Chen, Yao Lie of the Vanguard, Yao Bao’an of the Left Guard, Cavalier Attendant Wang Bo, Yao Jin, General Who Establishes Martial Might, Yao Hao, General Who Displays Might, Sun Xuan, right assistant director of the Department of State Affairs, and others all died in battle. Hong returned to the palace alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chen; Yao Lie of the Vanguard; Yao Bao'an of the Left Guard; Cavalier Attendant Wang Bo; General Who Establishes Martial Might Yao Jin; General Who Displays Might Yao Hao; Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Sun Xuan; and the others all died in battle. Yao Hong rode back to the palace alone.

sentences.zh: 鎮惡入自平朔門，泓與姚裕等數百騎出奔于石橋。

translations.literal: Zhen'e entered from Pingshuo Gate; Hong with Yao Yu and several hundred horse fled out toward Stone Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen’e entered through Pingshuo Gate. Yao Hong, Yao Yu and the others fled with several hundred horsemen to Stone Bridge.

sentences.zh: 贊聞泓之敗也，召將士告之，眾皆以刀擊地，攘袂大泣。

translations.literal: When Zan heard of Hong's defeat, he summoned officers and soldiers and told them; all struck the earth with knives, pulled sleeves and wept greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Zan learned of Hong’s defeat, he summoned his officers and men and told them. They all struck the ground with their knives, pushed up their sleeves and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 胡翼度先與劉裕陰通，是日棄眾奔裕。

translations.literal: Hu Yidu had earlier secretly communicated with Liu Yu; that day he abandoned the host and fled to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Yidu had already been in secret contact with Liu Yu. That day he abandoned his men and fled to Yu.

sentences.zh: 贊夜率諸軍，將會泓于石橋，王師已固諸門，贊軍不得入，眾皆驚散。

translations.literal: Zan by night led all armies, planning to join Hong at Stone Bridge; the royal army had already secured all gates; Zan's army could not enter; the host all startled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: That night Yao Zan led the armies out to join Hong at Stone Bridge. The Jin army already held all the gates. Zan’s army could not enter, and his men scattered in alarm.

sentences.zh: 泓計無所出，謀欲降於裕。

translations.literal: Hong had no plan left, plotted wishing to surrender to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At a loss for any other plan, Yao Hong considered surrendering to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 其子佛念，年十一，謂泓曰：「晉人將逞其欲，終必不全，願自裁決。」

translations.literal: His eleven-year-old son Fonian said to Hong, “The men of Jin will have their way. In the end there will surely be no escape. Death by one’s own hand would be better.”
translations.idiomatic: His eleven-year-old son Fonian said to Hong, “The men of Jin will have their way. In the end there will surely be no escape. Death by one’s own hand would be better.”

sentences.zh: 泓憮然不答。

translations.literal: Hong looked mournful and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong was stricken and gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 佛念遂登宮牆自投而死。

translations.literal: Fonian then climbed the palace wall and threw himself down to die.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Fonian then climbed the palace wall and threw himself to his death.

sentences.zh: 泓將妻子詣壘門而降。

translations.literal: Hong led wife and children to the camp gate and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Hong took his wife and children to the gate of the Jin camp and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 贊率宗室子弟百餘人亦降於裕，裕盡殺之，余宗遷於江南。

translations.literal: Zan led more than a hundred sons and nephews of the imperial clan also to surrender to Yu; Yu killed them all; the rest of the clan was moved south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Zan also surrendered to Liu Yu, leading more than a hundred younger men of the imperial clan. Liu Yu killed them all. The rest of the clan was moved south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 送泓于建康市斬之，時年三十，在位二年。

translations.literal: They sent Hong to Jiankang and beheaded him in the marketplace. He was thirty years old and had been on the throne for two years.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong was sent to Jiankang and beheaded in the marketplace. He was thirty years old and had reigned for two years.

sentences.zh: 建康百里之內，草木皆燋死焉。

translations.literal: Within a hundred li of Jiankang, grass and trees all scorched dead.
translations.idiomatic: Within a hundred li of Jiankang, grass and trees all scorched dead.

sentences.zh: 姚萇以孝武太元九年僭立，至泓三世，以安帝義熙十三年而滅，凡三十二年。

translations.literal: Yao Chang presumptuously rose in the ninth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu; down to Hong three generations; in the thirteenth year of Yixi under Emperor An they perished—thirty-two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From Yao Chang's usurpation in the ninth year of Taiyuan under Emperor Xiaowu to the fall in the thirteenth year of Yixi under Emperor An, the Later Qin lasted three reigns and thirty-two years.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historical Appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historical Appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自長江徙禦，化龍創業，巨寇乘機而未寧，戎馬交馳而不息，晦重氛於六漠，鼓洪流於八際，天未厭亂，凶旅實繁。

translations.literal: The court historian says: Ever since the imperial court moved to the Yangtze and the prince of the dragon prophecy founded his dynasty there, great raiders have seized their opportunity and refused to be still. Warhorses have galloped to and fro without rest. Dense darkness shrouded the six reaches of the world, and great floods surged to its eight limits. Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and violent armies were many indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The court historian says: Ever since the imperial court moved to the Yangtze and the prince of the dragon prophecy founded his dynasty there, great raiders have seized their opportunity and refused to be still. Warhorses have galloped to and fro without rest. Dense darkness shrouded the six reaches of the world, and great floods surged to its eight limits. Heaven had not yet tired of disorder, and violent armies were many indeed.

sentences.zh: 弋仲越自金方，言歸石氏，抗直詞於暴主，闡忠訓于危朝，貽厥之謀，在乎歸順，鳴哀之義，有足稱焉。

translations.literal: Yao Yizhong came from the west and gave his allegiance to the Shi house. He spoke frankly to its violent ruler Shi Hu and gave loyal counsel at a court in peril. The plan he left his descendants was to submit to Jin. The righteousness of his dying words deserves praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yizhong came from the west and gave his allegiance to the Shi house. He spoke frankly to its violent ruler Shi Hu and gave loyal counsel at a court in peril. The plan he left his descendants was to submit to Jin. The righteousness of his dying words deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 景國弱歲英奇，見方孫策，詳其幹識，無忝斯言，遂踐迷途，良可悲矣！

translations.literal: Jingguo in weak years was heroic and strange, compared to Sun Ce; examining his capacity and insight, he did not shame that saying—yet he trod a lost road, truly lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang, called Jingguo, showed exceptional courage and talent from his youth and was compared to Sun Ce. A close look at his ability and judgment bears out the comparison. That he went on to take a mistaken path is indeed cause for sorrow.

sentences.zh: 景茂因仲襄之緒，躡苻亡之會，嘯命群豪，恢弘霸業，假容沖之銳，俯定函、秦；

translations.literal: Yao Chang, called Jingmao, took up the work left by Yao Yizhong and Yao Xiang. Seizing the occasion of the Fu house’s collapse, he called the regional leaders to his side and extended his dominion. Drawing on the force of Murong Chong’s attack, he secured Hangu and the Qin lands with ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang, called Jingmao, took up the work left by Yao Yizhong and Yao Xiang. Seizing the occasion of the Fu house’s collapse, he called the regional leaders to his side and extended his dominion. Drawing on the force of Murong Chong’s attack, he secured Hangu and the Qin lands with ease.

sentences.zh: 挫雷惡之鋒，載甯東北。

translations.literal: He blunted Lei Edi’s attack and brought peace to the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: He blunted Lei Edi’s attack and brought peace to the northeast.

sentences.zh: 在茲奸略，實冠凶徒。

translations.literal: In these crafty stratagems he truly crowned the villains.
translations.idiomatic: In cunning he outdid every rival warlord.

sentences.zh: 列樹而表新營，雖云效績；

translations.literal: He had trees planted in rows to mark his new camp. That, to be sure, commemorated an achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He had trees planted in rows to mark his new camp. That, to be sure, commemorated an achievement.

sentences.zh: 薦棘而陵舊主，何其不仁！

translations.literal: But to lay the body of his former lord Fu Jian on thorns and dishonor him in that way—what cruelty!
translations.idiomatic: But to lay the body of his former lord Fu Jian on thorns and dishonor him in that way—what cruelty!

sentences.zh: 安枕而終，斯為幸也。

translations.literal: To pillow in peace and end—this was fortune.
translations.idiomatic: He died in bed—that was luck enough.

sentences.zh: 子略克摧勍敵，荷成先構，虛襟訪道，側席求賢，敦友弟以睦其親，明賞罰以臨其下，英髦盡節，爪牙畢命。

translations.literal: Yao Xing, called Zilüe, crushed powerful enemies and carried forward the work his predecessor had begun. With an open mind he sought instruction and made room at his side for worthy men. His affection for his brothers brought harmony to the family, and he governed his subjects by clear rewards and punishments. Men of talent served him with complete devotion, and his fighting men gave their lives for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing, called Zilüe, crushed powerful enemies and carried forward the work his predecessor had begun. With an open mind he sought instruction and made room at his side for worthy men. His affection for his brothers brought harmony to the family, and he governed his subjects by clear rewards and punishments. Men of talent served him with complete devotion, and his fighting men gave their lives for him.

sentences.zh: 取汾、絳，陷許、洛，款僭燕而籓偽蜀，夷隴右而靜河西，俗阜年豐，遠安邇輯，雖楚莊、秦穆何以加焉！

translations.literal: He took Fen and Jiang and captured Xu and Luo, won the submission of the usurping Yan regime and made the pretended regime in Shu his vassal. He subdued Longyou and pacified Hexi. The people prospered, harvests were plentiful, distant regions were secure and those nearby were united. How could King Zhuang of Chu or Duke Mu of Qin have surpassed him?
translations.idiomatic: He took Fen and Jiang and captured Xu and Luo. He won the allegiance of the rival Yan regime and made the regime in Shu his vassal. He subdued Longyou and pacified Hexi. The people prospered, the harvests were plentiful, distant regions were secure and those close at hand were united. How could King Zhuang of Chu or Duke Mu of Qin have surpassed him?

sentences.zh: 既而逞志矜功，弗虞後患。

translations.literal: Yet afterward he indulged his will and boasted of merit, did not guard against later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he gave free rein to his ambitions and boasted of his achievements, taking no thought for future trouble.

sentences.zh: 委涼都於禿髮，授朔方於赫連，專己生災，邊城繼陷，距諫招禍，蕭牆屢發，戰無寧歲，人有危心。

translations.literal: He entrusted the capital of Liang to Tufa and granted Shuofang to Helian. His insistence on having his way bred disasters. Frontier cities fell in succession, and his rejection of remonstrance invited calamity. Trouble repeatedly broke out within his own house. There was no year of respite from warfare, and the people felt themselves in danger.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted the Liang capital to Tufa and handed Shuofang to Helian, trusting himself bred disaster; border cities fell in succession, rejecting remonstrance invited calamity, inner-wall strife broke out again and again, war had no quiet year, and men lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 豈宜騁彼雄圖，被深恩於介士；

translations.literal: With such grand designs to pursue, should he not have shown profound favor to his men-at-arms?
translations.idiomatic: With such grand designs to pursue, should he not have shown profound favor to his men-at-arms?

sentences.zh: 翻崇詭說，加殊禮于桑門！

translations.literal: yet he reversed course to honor crafty doctrine and piled special rites on shaven monks!
translations.idiomatic: Instead he exalted teachings the historian deemed deceptive and paid exceptional honors to Buddhist monks.

sentences.zh: 當有為之時，肄無為之業，麗衣腴食，殆將萬數，析實談空，靡然成俗。

translations.literal: At a time that demanded action he devoted himself to the pursuit of nonaction. Those clad in fine robes and fed on rich food numbered nearly ten thousand. Analyzing the real and discoursing on emptiness became the general fashion.
translations.idiomatic: At a time that demanded action he devoted himself to the pursuit of nonaction. Those clad in fine robes and fed on rich food numbered nearly ten thousand. Analyzing the real and discoursing on emptiness became the general fashion.

sentences.zh: 夫以漢朝殷廣，猶鄙鴻都之費；

translations.literal: Even Han's vast abundance still despised Hongdu's expense;
translations.idiomatic: Even under the wealthy and far-reaching Han dynasty, the expense of the Hongdu academy drew scorn.

sentences.zh: 況乎偽境日侵，寧堪永貴之役！

translations.literal: How much less could a usurping regime, its borders daily encroached upon, bear the labor of construction at Yonggui?
translations.idiomatic: How, then, could a realm whose borders were daily encroached upon bear the cost of building the Buddhist stupa at Yonggui?

sentences.zh: 儲用殫竭，山林有稅，政荒威挫，職是之由，坐致淪胥，非天喪也。

translations.literal: Stores were exhausted, hills and forests taxed; government wild, awe broken—this is the reason; sitting to bring ruin—Heaven did not destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Reserves were exhausted, and even the hills and forests were taxed. Government fell into neglect and authority was broken. These were the causes. They brought ruin upon themselves; Heaven did not destroy them.

sentences.zh: 元子以庸懦之質，屬傾擾之餘，內難方殷，外禦斯輟。

translations.literal: Yuanzi with a mediocre and timid substance, amid the aftermath of overturn and turmoil, inner disaster just raging, outer defense then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hong, called Yuanzi, was mediocre and timid. He came to power in the aftermath of upheaval, and as internal troubles intensified, defense against outside enemies ceased.

sentences.zh: 王師杖順，弭節而下長安；

translations.literal: With right on its side, the Jin army advanced at an easy pace and took Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: With right on its side, the Jin army advanced at an easy pace and took Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 凶嗣失圖，系組而降軹道。

translations.literal: The wicked heir lost his plan and surrendered with a cord about his neck, as the Qin ruler had at Zhidao.
translations.idiomatic: The wicked heir, at a loss for any plan, surrendered with the cord about his neck, like the Qin ruler at Zhidao.

sentences.zh: 物極則反，抑斯之謂歟！

translations.literal: Things extreme then reverse—does this say it!
translations.idiomatic: When things reach their extreme, they reverse course. Is this what the saying means?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：弋仲剛烈，終表奇節。

translations.literal: Eulogy says: Yizhong was stern and fierce, in the end displayed a strange integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Yao Yizhong was stern and fierce, and in the end displayed remarkable integrity.

sentences.zh: 襄實英果，萇惟奸傑。

translations.literal: Xiang was indeed heroic and resolute; Chang was an outstanding man of treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xiang was truly heroic and resolute; Yao Chang was a treacherous champion.

sentences.zh: 興始崇構，泓遂摧滅。

translations.literal: Under Xing the dynastic edifice rose high; under Hong it came crashing down.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xing the dynastic edifice rose high; under Hong it came crashing down.

sentences.zh: 貽誡將來，無踐危轍。

translations.literal: Leave warning to those who come—do not tread this perilous rut.
translations.idiomatic: Let this stand as a warning to those who come after: do not follow the same perilous tracks.
